title: Disentangling Total-Variance and Signal-to-Noise-Ratio Improves Diffusion Models
abstract: arXiv:2502.08598v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Diffusion models have been widely adopted as a powerful generative framework across numerous scientific domains, yet their inherently iterative sampling process remains a significant computational bottleneck. While this is typically mitigated by reducing the number of reverse diffusion steps, sample quality becomes highly sensitive to the chosen noise schedule, i.e. the manner in which noise is introduced and the signal is reduced at each step. Although prior work has improved on the original variance-preserving and variance-exploding schedules, these approaches passively adjust the total variance, without direct independent control over it. In this work, we propose a novel total-variance/signal-to-noise-ratio disentangled (TV/SNR) framework, where TV and SNR can be controlled independently. tldr: 提出了一种总方差/信噪比解耦（TV/SNR）框架，使扩散模型噪声调度中的总方差和信噪比可被独立控制，并发现恒定总方差调度能够持续改进指数爆炸总方差的调度。
en_tdlr: Proposes a novel total-variance/signal-to-noise-ratio disentangled (TV/SNR) framework that enables independent control of total variance and SNR in diffusion model noise schedules, revealing that constant-TV schedules consistently improve exponentially exploding-TV schedules.
